extraFacts.fact: NPSM is a straight (parallel) pipe thread for free-fitting mechanical joints under ASME B1.20.1; it does not seal on the thread but on a gasket or seat. NPSH is the straight hose-coupling thread (ASME B1.20.7) and NST is the National Standard Thread used on fire hose couplings (NFPA 1963); these couplings seal on a gasket.
extraFacts.source: ASME B1.20.1; ASME B1.20.7 Hose Coupling Screw Threads; NFPA 1963 Fire Hose Connections

extraFacts.fact: NPT is a tapered pipe thread standardised in ASME B1.20.1; NPTF (Dryseal) is standardised in ASME B1.20.3 and is cut so the crests and roots close up as the joint is tightened, so it seals on the thread.
extraFacts.source: ASME B1.20.1 and ASME B1.20.3 scopes

extraFacts.fact: SAE J514 is the standard for 37° flared (JIC) tube fittings, whose flare seats on a 74° included cone; the 45° SAE flare is a different seat that does not mate with the 37° one.
Sixteenths of an inch: hose and fitting dash sizes count sixteenths, so -4 is 1/4 inch, -6 is 3/8 inch, -8 is 1/2 inch, -12 is 3/4 inch and -16 is 1 inch.
extraFacts.source: SAE J514 / ISO 8434 dash size convention

faqs.q: What is the Dixon 90 Degree Push-on Elbows, Female 37 Degree JIC/45 Degree SAE Swivel used for?

faqs.q: How do I read the part numbers of the Dixon 90 Degree Push-on Elbows, Female 37 Degree JIC/45 Degree SAE Swivel, such as 2890407C?
faqs.a: The four digits before the letter are sizes in sixteenths of an inch: in 2890407C, 04 is the 1/4" size and 07 is the 7/16-20 thread; in 2891217C, 12 is 3/4" and 17 is the 1-1/16-12 thread. A trailing SAE, as in 2890610CSAE, marks the SAE 45° seat version.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Dixon 90 Degree Push-on Elbows, Female 37 Degree JIC/45 Degree SAE Swivel range cover?
faqs.a: The range holds 6 part numbers: 2890407C (1/4"), 2890609C (3/8"), 2890812C (1/2"), 2891217C (3/4"), plus 2890610CSAE and 2890407CSAE for the SAE 45° seat. The Sizes & Part Numbers table lists each one with its swivel thread.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right Dixon 90 Degree Push-on Elbows, Female 37 Degree JIC/45 Degree SAE Swivel for my hose or port?
faqs.a: Match two things: the hose size and the swivel thread on the mating part. 3/8" push-on hose, for example, comes with a 9/16-18 JIC thread (2890609C) or a 5/8-18 SAE thread (2890610CSAE), so check the seat angle, 37° or 45°, before ordering.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature does the Dixon 90 Degree Push-on Elbows, Female 37 Degree JIC/45 Degree SAE Swivel take?
faqs.a: The maker states 350 psi (24 bar) for every part number in this range, with an operating temperature of -40°F to +150°F. A push-on joint holds only what the hose and the barb allow, so use it with push-on hose rated for that pressure.

faqs.q: What material is the Dixon 90 Degree Push-on Elbows, Female 37 Degree JIC/45 Degree SAE Swivel made from?
faqs.a: The range is steel, as the maker lists it, with UNF threads on the swivel end. Ask us for the plating or stainless option if the elbow will see weather or washdown.

faqs.q: Which standards and thread types apply to the Dixon 90 Degree Push-on Elbows, Female 37 Degree JIC/45 Degree SAE Swivel?
faqs.a: The swivel ends use UNF threads and a JIC 37° or SAE 45° flare seat, as the listing states; both seats are flared and metal-to-metal. The 37° and 45° seats do not mate with each other, so confirm the angle of your port.

faqs.q: What does the Dixon 90 Degree Push-on Elbows, Female 37 Degree JIC/45 Degree SAE Swivel connect to?

faqs.q: How should I fit and inspect the Dixon 90 Degree Push-on Elbows, Female 37 Degree JIC/45 Degree SAE Swivel?

faqs.q: What does the Dixon Instrumentation Male Elbows connect to?
faqs.a: The male NPT end goes into a female NPT port and the other end takes the instrument tube. For a straight connection use the [Dixon Instrumentation Male Connectors](/p/dixon-instrumentation-male-connectors).

faqs.q: How should I fit and inspect the Dixon Instrumentation Male Elbows?
faqs.a: Seal the thread with sealant, position the elbow by turning it into the port, and do not back it off to align it, as that breaks the seal. Re-check after the first thermal cycle.

faqs.q: When should I choose the Dixon Instrumentation Male Elbows instead of the male connectors?
faqs.a: Choose the elbows, listed in 8 part numbers, where the tube must turn through 90° at the port, and the [Dixon Instrumentation Male Connectors](/p/dixon-instrumentation-male-connectors), listed in 17, where it runs straight. The material and temperature range are the same.

faqs.q: What is the Dixon Male JIC 37 Degree Flare x Male Metric Parallel Thread Adapters used for?

faqs.q: How do I read the part numbers of the Dixon Male JIC 37 Degree Flare x Male Metric Parallel Thread Adapters, such as M7400-16-33?
faqs.a: In M7400-6-16 the 6 is the JIC flare size (9/16-18) and 16 is the metric thread diameter in millimetres (M16 x 1.5); M7400-16-33 is a 1-5/16-12 flare with an M33 x 2 thread. The rows give both threads for each number.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Dixon Male JIC 37 Degree Flare x Male Metric Parallel Thread Adapters range cover?
faqs.a: Eight part numbers are listed, such as M7400-4-10 (7/16-20 to M10 x 1), M7400-6-14, M7400-6-16, M7400-8-16, M7400-12-22, M7400-12-27 and M7400-16-33. The Sizes & Part Numbers table gives both threads.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right Dixon Male JIC 37 Degree Flare x Male Metric Parallel Thread Adapters for my hose or port?
faqs.a: Identify the JIC size and the metric thread: 9/16-18 can go to M14 x 1.5 (M7400-6-14) or M16 x 1.5 (M7400-6-16), and 1 1/16-12 can go to M22 x 1.5 or M27 x 2. Measure the metric port to confirm the pitch.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature does the Dixon Male JIC 37 Degree Flare x Male Metric Parallel Thread Adapters take?
faqs.a: The listing states no pressure rating for this range. A flared and parallel-thread joint holds what the weaker end and the sealing method allow, so tell us the working pressure and we will confirm it before you order.

faqs.q: What material is the Dixon Male JIC 37 Degree Flare x Male Metric Parallel Thread Adapters made from?
faqs.a: The range is steel, as the listing states. Ask us if you need a plated or stainless version for a corrosive environment.

faqs.q: Which standards and thread types apply to the Dixon Male JIC 37 Degree Flare x Male Metric Parallel Thread Adapters?
faqs.a: The flare end is JIC 37°, as the listing states, and the other end is a metric parallel thread such as M16 x 1.5. A parallel metric thread is not sealed by the thread, so the joint needs a face seal or washer on the metric port.

faqs.q: What does the Dixon Male JIC 37 Degree Flare x Male Metric Parallel Thread Adapters connect to?
faqs.a: The JIC end mates with a female JIC swivel nut and the metric end screws into a metric parallel port. See the [metric hose fittings shelf](/c/metric-hose-fittings) and the [JIC 37° hose fittings shelf](/c/jic-37-hose-fittings).

faqs.q: How should I fit and inspect the Dixon Male JIC 37 Degree Flare x Male Metric Parallel Thread Adapters?
faqs.a: Check the metric port style, whether it takes a bonded washer, an O-ring or a cone seat, before fitting. Seat the JIC flare square and tighten by the make-up turns for the size.

faqs.q: How does the Dixon Male JIC 37 Degree Flare x Male Metric Parallel adapter compare with the Dixon Male x Male NPTF Flat Face connectors?

faqs.q: How do I read the part numbers of the Dixon Nipples, such as 3501?

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Dixon Nipples range cover?
faqs.a: The 41 part numbers include steel male nipples from 1/4 to 1 inch NPT, female FNPT nipples such as 3546 and 3554, brass nipples BR1M1 and BR1GM1, polypropylene nipples 62192 to 62226 and octagonal nipples OCTOE32. The Sizes & Part Numbers table lists each.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right Dixon Nipples for my hose or port?
faqs.a: Decide the material first, then the thread on each end: 3512 is zinc-plated steel 1/2 x 1/2 MNPT, 62225 is 1 inch MNPT polypropylene at 4 inch overall length and BR1GM2-B-E-7 is brass with a 1/4 male BSPP thread. Send the thread and length if a size is not obvious.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature does the Dixon Nipples take?

faqs.q: What material is the Dixon Nipples made from?
faqs.a: The range mixes materials: zinc-plated steel, brass, carbon steel, polypropylene and cast brass. The material is shown in each row's description, so choose by part number, not by the listing title alone.

faqs.q: Which standards and thread types apply to the Dixon Nipples?
faqs.a: The listing gives NPT and NPTF taper threads, plus BSPP and metric ends on some brass nipples. NPT and NPTF look alike but NPTF is the Dryseal form that seals on the thread; keep BSPP away from NPT ports.

faqs.q: What does the Dixon Nipples connect to?
faqs.a: A nipple joins two female ports; steel ones suit hydraulic and general pipe work, and brass ones suit instrument and air lines. The [Dixon Hex Pipe Nipples](/p/dixon-hex-pipe-nipples) have a hex and a pressure rating by size.

faqs.q: How should I fit and inspect the Dixon Nipples?
faqs.a: Seal tapered threads with a sealant suited to the fluid, hand-start the thread and finish with a spanner. Do not mix steel and polypropylene parts in one joint, as the plastic threads strip easily.

faqs.q: What is the Dixon NPT Threaded One End Pipe Fittings used for?

faqs.q: How do I read the part numbers of the Dixon NPT Threaded One End Pipe Fittings, such as PN750?
faqs.a: The digits after PN are the size in thousandths: PN250 is 1/4", PN750 is 3/4", PN2000 is 2" and PN4000-series sizes go to 4". PNS means 304 stainless, as in PNS1500 (1-1/2"), and APN means aluminium, as in APN4000.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Dixon NPT Threaded One End Pipe Fittings range cover?

faqs.q: How do I choose the right Dixon NPT Threaded One End Pipe Fittings for my hose or port?
faqs.a: Choose the pipe size and the material together: PN1000 is a 1" carbon steel fitting, PNS1000 is the 304 stainless one and APN3000 is a 3" aluminium fitting. Match the size to the hose I.D. as well as the NPT port.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature does the Dixon NPT Threaded One End Pipe Fittings take?

faqs.q: What material is the Dixon NPT Threaded One End Pipe Fittings made from?
faqs.a: The listing names three materials: carbon steel (PN), 304 stainless steel (PNS) and aluminium (APN). Choose stainless for washdown or chemicals and aluminium where weight matters.

faqs.q: Which standards and thread types apply to the Dixon NPT Threaded One End Pipe Fittings?

faqs.q: What does the Dixon NPT Threaded One End Pipe Fittings connect to?

faqs.q: How do I choose the right Dixon Push On Hose Barbs for my hose or port?
faqs.a: Match the push-on hose I.D. and the end style: 2920608C is a 3/8" hose with a female rigid SAE 1/2-20, 2900508C is a 5/16" hose with a male SAE swivel and 2941212C is a 3/4" hose with a 3/4" rigid tube end.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature does the Dixon Push On Hose Barbs take?
faqs.a: The maker states 350 psi (24 bar) on five of the six rows and -40°F to +150°F for the range. 2861217CBC carries no stated rating, so ask us for it. Push-on joints suit only hose rated for that pressure.

faqs.q: What material is the Dixon Push On Hose Barbs made from?

faqs.q: How should I fit and inspect the Dixon Push On Hose Barbs?

faqs.q: What is the Dixon Style N35 Double Female Swivel Rocker Lugs used for?

faqs.q: How do I read the part numbers of the Dixon Style N35 Double Female Swivel Rocker Lugs, such as N35-15S15F?

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Dixon Style N35 Double Female Swivel Rocker Lugs range cover?

faqs.q: How do I choose the right Dixon Style N35 Double Female Swivel Rocker Lugs for my hose or port?

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature does the Dixon Style N35 Double Female Swivel Rocker Lugs take?

faqs.q: What material is the Dixon Style N35 Double Female Swivel Rocker Lugs made from?

faqs.q: Which standards and thread types apply to the Dixon Style N35 Double Female Swivel Rocker Lugs?

faqs.q: What does the Dixon Style N35 Double Female Swivel Rocker Lugs connect to?

faqs.q: How should I fit and inspect the Dixon Style N35 Double Female Swivel Rocker Lugs?
